post_understanding.summary: Wrapping a NOT EXISTS anti-semi-join predicate inside an IF EXISTS check in a stored procedure causes a dramatic slowdown in SQL Server. The EXISTS wrapper introduces a row goal, leading the optimizer to choose a nested loops plan (and often remove parallelism) instead of a parallel hash anti semi-join, resulting in much longer execution time.
symptoms: Plain SELECT version completes in ~3 seconds
Execution plan switches to Nested Loops and loses parallelism when wrapped in IF EXISTS
SELECT version uses Hash Match and parallelism
suspected_root_causes: Optimizer row goal introduced by EXISTS leading to plan regression
Join strategy change from Hash Anti Semi-Join to Nested Loops
Potential absence or suboptimal index on smalltable.source amplifying nested loop inner work
Parallelism removed due to row goal and costing, further slowing execution
Parameter sniffing and/or CE/version settings could exacerbate differences
key_evidence: Author reports 3 seconds for SELECT vs 10 minutes for IF EXISTS with identical predicate
Shared plans show slow plan with nested loops and no parallelism; fast plan with hash match and parallelism
Reference to Paul White's row goals analysis explaining EXISTS behavior
Answer guidance suggesting EXISTS/NOT EXISTS can cause row goals and loop joins
assumptions: Assumption: SQL Server 2012 (compatibility level 110) as tagged; old CE is in use
Assumption: bigtable is large (tens of millions of rows) with a substantial subset for databasename = 'someval'
Assumption: smalltable contains almost all source values present in bigtable except for a small fraction (to make NOT EXISTS result small)
Assumption: bigtable has an index supporting filtering on databasename (e.g., (databasename, source))
Assumption: smalltable has either no efficient index on source or statistics skew such that a nested loops inner probe is costly; this increases the contrast between hash vs loops
Assumption: Cost Threshold for Parallelism and MAXDOP settings allow parallel plans for the SELECT variant but the row goal discourages parallelism for IF EXISTS
Assumption: Queries use the same parameter values when comparing variants; parameter sniffing not intentionally mitigated

target_tables.purpose: Large fact table providing many candidate rows filtered by databasename and joined on source, to emphasize join strategy differences.

columns.name: source
columns.role: join key to smalltable; anti-semi-join predicate

columns.name: payload
columns.role: row size filler to mimic real width

generated_data_plan.distribution: databasename = 'someval' for ~20% of rows; remaining rows have other databasename values. source values drawn from 1,000,000 distinct strings; uniform-ish distribution; 'kt' appears in ~1% of rows to make l.source <> 'kt' filter non-trivial.
generated_data_plan.rationale: Large outer input with a moderately selective filter and many duplicate source values encourages a parallel hash anti semi-join for the SELECT variant. This volume makes a nested loops plan (induced by EXISTS row goal) significantly slower.

target_tables.purpose: Dimension-like table containing most source values to support the NOT EXISTS anti-semi-join and demonstrate performance sensitivity to join strategy.

columns.name: source
columns.role: join key; presence/absence determines NOT EXISTS result

generated_data_plan.distribution: Contains nearly all of the 1,000,000 possible source values except ~1,000 values intentionally omitted to create a small NOT EXISTS result set.
generated_data_plan.rationale: A nearly complete set ensures the anti-join result is small (rare NOT EXISTS matches). This pattern highlights that a hash anti semi-join is efficient while a nested loops plan must perform many inner checks, which is much slower without an index on source.

anomaly_injection.name: baseline_fast_select_with_not_exists
anomaly_injection.method: Run the SELECT version returning a result set; capture plan and timings.

parameters.sql: SELECT l.databasename FROM dbo.bigtable AS l WHERE l.databasename = @dbname AND l.source <> 'kt' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.smalltable AS c WHERE c.source = l.source);
indexes: CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_bigtable_databasename_source ON dbo.bigtable(databasename, source) INCLUDE (id);
parameters.note: Do not create an index on dbo.smalltable(source) initially to maximize the plan contrast; optionally test with it later.

safety_notes: Limit result set retrieval if client memory is constrained.
Ensure STATISTICS IO/TIME only; do not enable SET options that change semantics.

anomaly_injection.name: plan_regression_via_if_exists_row_goal
anomaly_injection.method: Wrap the same predicate in an IF EXISTS to introduce a row goal; observe plan change to Nested Loops and loss of parallelism.

parameters.sql: IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.bigtable AS l WHERE l.databasename = @dbname AND l.source <> 'kt' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.smalltable AS c WHERE c.source = l.source)) BEGIN RAISERROR('Source missing',16,1); RETURN; END
parameters.expected_plan_shape: Nested Loops outer input on bigtable (filtered on databasename), inner probes/scan on smalltable; no parallelism.

safety_notes: This may run for several minutes on large data; be prepared to cancel if it exceeds resource budget.
Monitor CPU and I/O to avoid impacting other workloads (run on isolated test server).

anomaly_injection.name: amplify_difference_by_index_toggle_optional
anomaly_injection.method: Optionally toggle an index on smalltable(source) to study impact on nested loops vs hash anti-join performance and plan selection.

parameters.create_index: CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_smalltable_source ON dbo.smalltable(source);
parameters.drop_index: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS IX_smalltable_source ON dbo.smalltable;
parameters.phases: Run baseline and IF EXISTS both with and without IX_smalltable_source.

safety_notes: Index create/drop on large tables can be resource-intensive; use ONLINE = ON if edition supports, or keep table small enough for safe ops.
Ensure repeatable environment when comparing (clear cache between runs or use fresh connection).

anomaly_injection.name: force_expected_join_behaviors_for_validation_optional
anomaly_injection.method: Use join hints as a diagnostic only: OPTION (HASH JOIN) for the SELECT; OPTION (LOOP JOIN) for the IF EXISTS to confirm join strategy explains timing difference.

parameters.select_hint_sql: SELECT l.databasename FROM dbo.bigtable AS l WHERE l.databasename = @dbname AND l.source <> 'kt' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.smalltable AS c WHERE c.source = l.source) OPTION (HASH JOIN);
parameters.if_exists_hint_sql: IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.bigtable AS l WHERE l.databasename = @dbname AND l.source <> 'kt' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.smalltable AS c WHERE c.source = l.source) OPTION (LOOP JOIN)) BEGIN RAISERROR('Source missing',16,1); RETURN; END

safety_notes: Hints alter optimizer choices; use only for validation and do not leave in production.
Ensure you revert to hint-free queries for the main comparison.

metrics.expected_change: IF EXISTS variant increases by at least 10x compared to SELECT variant
likely increase for IF EXISTS (less parallelism) despite similar logical work
significant increase for IF EXISTS due to repeated smalltable scans/seeks under nested loops
SELECT shows >1 (parallel); IF EXISTS shows 1 (no parallelism)
SELECT uses Hash Match (Anti Semi Join) with parallel operators; IF EXISTS uses Nested Loops with inner scans/seeks

query_or_transaction_effects: The SELECT variant returns a small result set quickly.
The IF EXISTS variant either runs for several minutes before raising the error or shows robust slowdown immediately.
With a smalltable(source) index present, both may improve, but IF EXISTS still shows nested loops and remains slower relative to SELECT.
validation_criteria: Reproduction is considered matched if the IF EXISTS form produces a nested loops, non-parallel plan and is at least an order of magnitude slower than the SELECT form on the same dataset and parameters.
STATISTICS IO/TIME indicate many more reads or inner operations against smalltable for IF EXISTS.
Removing the EXISTS wrapper (or using LEFT JOIN/EXCEPT) restores a hash anti semi-join and fast execution.

open_questions: What are the exact row counts and data distributions for bigtable and smalltable (cardinality, number of distinct source values, percentage of 'someval' and 'kt')?
What indexes exist on bigtable(databasename, source) and smalltable(source)? Are there filtered indexes or included columns?
Which SQL Server version/build and database compatibility level are/were used? Is the old or new cardinality estimator in effect?
Are there any query or database-level options affecting parallelism (MAXDOP, Cost Threshold for Parallelism, Resource Governor)?
Are parameters fixed literals or parameterized? Is parameter sniffing a factor inside the stored procedure?
Do the shared plans show any spools or additional predicates in the slow plan beyond the nested loops?
Is smalltable frequently updated, and are its statistics up to date? Any auto-created stats on source?
Is the slow behavior consistent across executions or intermittent (e.g., cache warm vs cold)?
